Reports identify amounts, source/country and purpose or intended use. Restricted or conditional gifts also require amounts, dates, conditions, and specified source-country information.

A state or other federal report can replace the disclosure report only if it contains all required information for the same or an equivalent period; state assurances may be required. Institutions must be able to revise past reports to correct errors.

For a knowing or willful disclosure or agreement-copy/translation violation, the Secretary may impose $250 to 50% of the gift or contract amount; three consecutive years permit an additional fine of $100,000 to the gift or contract amount. Knowing or willful foreign-ownership-report violations can incur up to 25% of Higher Education Act funding excluding Title IV student aid, with an additional fine subject to the same 25% cap for three consecutive years of violations. Administrative errors lasting three consecutive years can incur $250 to 50% of the gift or contract amount; two consecutive years without the required gift/contract report can trigger a compliance plan. These are the printed statutory bounds, not a prediction of penalties imposed.

Excluded transactions include student-attendance payments or scholarships from a natural person acting individually, not for another person or entity except the student, without another contract beyond the institution-student attendance agreement; specified intellectual-property licensing or technical assistance not identified as a national-security risk; and funds solely for clinical trials. A U.S.-located institution's purchases of property or services from a foreign source are outside the contract definition. Gifts and contracts through an institution's supporting entities are included. Restricted or conditional gifts/contracts include terms concerning faculty employment, academic or research units/programs, student selection/admission, or aid restricted by the listed country, religion, sex, ethnic-origin or political-opinion categories.

The amendment also incorporates HEA487(e)(2)(B)(ii) gift exceptions: loan/default-prevention/financial-literacy materials and programs; qualifying professional-training food, refreshments and materials; comparable student-employee loan benefits; institution-controlled, non-promotional loan counseling; specified lender/servicer/guarantor philanthropy or contributions without a loan-related advantage; and state-administered education aid. These categories retain the conditions in the incorporated statute, governed here in its 2024 U.S. Code edition.

Institutions must designate a compliance officer, and the Department must maintain an internal, conflict-free contact for compliance assistance and database improvements. Data sharing with outside persons, including political appointees and personnel detailed from other agencies, is limited to expressly authorized or public information. Database user-group composition and meeting mechanics are ancillary to the explanation, not absent from the governed evidence.

Negotiated rules must align with other agencies' reporting under the CHIPS Act, the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, and OSTP guidance including the specified NSPM-33 implementation guidance. Alignment is a rulemaking duty, not an assertion that all reporting regimes become identical. The substitute links Section 117's effective date to the regulations and separately specifies a database deadline relative to the first July 31 after enactment; this candidate does not invent a resolution of that timing interaction.
